report_name: DreamHost Confirms Months-Long Breach; Customer Credentials Stolen

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor responsible for the prolonged breach of DreamHost starting in August 2026, during which they stole customer emails and credentials.
threat_actors.goals: To steal customer credentials and other data from a web hosting provider for subsequent malicious use.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: The attackers stole customer emails and account credentials from DreamHost's systems during a prolonged breach that started in August 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The attackers successfully exfiltrated stolen customer data, including emails and credentials, over several months.

identities.name: DreamHost
identities.description: A major web hosting provider that was the victim of a prolonged cyberattack, resulting in the exfiltration of customer data including emails and account credentials.

indicators.name: LSASS Process Access For Credential Dumping
indicators.pattern:
title: LSASS Process Access For Credential Dumping
id: 2b93f8e1-7c9a-4b1f-9f3d-5e6a8b7c6d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects process access to LSASS memory, which may indicate credential dumping attempts such as those performed by Mimikatz. This activity is associated with OS Credential Dumping (T1003).
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-07
tags:
  - attack.t1003.001
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
  filter_legit:
    SourceImage|endswith:
      - '\svchost.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
      - '\wininit.exe'
      - '\csrss.exe'
      - '\vmwp.exe'
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
indicators.description: Detects process access to the LSASS process, a common technique for credential dumping (T1003). The article's cyber observables section noted patterns related to lsass.exe, indicating this behavior was relevant to the incident.

relationships.source_name: LSASS Process Access For Credential Dumping
